# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III, but this deadline has since been postponed through the "AI Omnibus" amendment process (high confidence). As of the consolidated text applicable from 27 July 2026, obligations for Annex III high-risk systems now apply from 2 December 2027, with a separate 2 August 2028 date for high-risk systems that are safety components of products under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) were scheduled to become subject to obligations from 2 August 2026 ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
The European Commission's Digital/AI Omnibus proposal sought to extend the Annex III application date by up to 16 months, linking the new start date to Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence). Political agreement on these amendments between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence). The Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence).

### Current Applicable Dates
Under the consolidated text applicable from 27 July 2026, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems (Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3, excluding Article 6(5)) now apply from **2 December 2027** ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Separately, high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products, or are themselves products, covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I will become subject to obligations from **2 August 2028** ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Both the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are described as "backstop" dates tied to Commission confirmation of standards and tools availability ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence).

### Legal Citation and Compliance Requirements
Some secondary sources refer to the amending instrument as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)), though this citation has low corroboration (low confidence). Separately, providers of Annex III high-risk systems are generally understood to need to meet requirements in Articles 8–15 and complete a conformity assessment before market placement ([Annex III high-risk AI obligations guide](https://ai-act-readiness.example/annex-iii-obligations-guide)), though this claim rests on a single, weakly-corroborated source (low confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between sources: several commentary pieces and guides (including some dated as late as April 2026) continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline ([CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)), while authoritative EU sources confirm the deadline has moved to 2 December 2027 following the Omnibus's entry into force ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This discrepancy likely reflects outdated content predating the Omnibus's finalization.

There is also ambiguity regarding whether 2 December 2027 is an absolute fixed date or remains conditional on Commission confirmation of standards — Council/Parliament communications frame it as conditional ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)), while the consolidated legal text presents it as a fixed calendar date ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (low confidence claims, flagged below).

Two claims fall below the 0.4 confidence threshold and should be treated cautiously: the citation of "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (0.14 confidence), the interpretation regarding the technical applicability of the original 2 August 2026 date absent Omnibus approval (0.12 confidence), and the Articles 8–15 conformity assessment claim (0.12 confidence).

## Knowledge Gaps
Key unresolved questions include: whether 2 December 2027 could still be adjusted if the Commission fails to confirm standards/tools readiness in time; whether specific Annex III use-case subcategories carry different sub-deadlines; the precise text and scope of the regulation amending Article 113; whether Article 6(1) and 6(5) classification provisions follow a distinct timeline from the rest of Chapter III; and how transition arrangements for AI systems already on the market interact with the revised 2027/2028 dates.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III, but this deadline has since been postponed through the "AI Omnibus" amendment process (high confidence). As of the consolidated text applicable from 27 July 2026, obligations for Annex III high-risk systems now apply from 2 December 2027, with a separate 2 August 2028 date for high-risk systems that are safety components of products under Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) were scheduled to become subject to obligations from 2 August 2026 ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
The European Commission's Digital/AI Omnibus proposal sought to extend the Annex III application date by up to 16 months, linking the new start date to Commission confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence). Political agreement on these amendments between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence). The Omnibus legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 and entered into force on 27 July 2026 ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)) (medium confidence).

### Current Applicable Dates
Under the consolidated text applicable from 27 July 2026, obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems (Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3, excluding Article 6(5)) now apply from **2 December 2027** ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Separately, high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products, or are themselves products, covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I will become subject to obligations from **2 August 2028** ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)) (high confidence). Both the 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 dates are described as "backstop" dates tied to Commission confirmation of standards and tools availability ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)) (high confidence).

### Legal Citation and Compliance Requirements
Some secondary sources refer to the amending instrument as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)), though this citation has low corroboration (low confidence). Separately, providers of Annex III high-risk systems are generally understood to need to meet requirements in Articles 8–15 and complete a conformity assessment before market placement, though this claim rests on a single, weakly-corroborated source (low confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between sources: several commentary pieces and guides (including some dated as late as April 2026) continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline ([CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)), while authoritative EU sources confirm the deadline has moved to 2 December 2027 following the Omnibus's entry into force ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This discrepancy likely reflects outdated content predating the Omnibus's finalization.

There is also ambiguity regarding whether 2 December 2027 is an absolute fixed date or remains conditional on Commission confirmation of standards — Council/Parliament communications frame it as conditional, while the consolidated legal text presents it as a fixed calendar date (low confidence claims, flagged below).

Two claims fall below the 0.4 confidence threshold and should be treated cautiously: the citation of "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (0.14 confidence) and the interpretation regarding the technical applicability of the original 2 August 2026 date absent Omnibus approval (0.12 confidence), as well as the Article 8-15 conformity assessment claim (0.12 confidence).

## Knowledge Gaps
Key unresolved questions include: whether 2 December 2027 could still be adjusted if the Commission fails to confirm standards/tools readiness in time; whether specific Annex III use-case subcategories carry different sub-deadlines; the precise text and scope of the regulation amending Article 113; whether Article 6(1) and 6(5) classification provisions follow a distinct timeline from the rest of Chapter III; and how transition arrangements for AI systems already on the market interact with the revised 2027/2028 dates.
